utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case Number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis for the Prosecution, assisted today by our intern, Daniella Rudy, and our case manager, Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. President. Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel, and Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we have the appearances for the other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and our legal assistant, Nermin Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. On the 18th of April, the 210th day of the proceedings, I would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom, the Prosecution, Defence counsel, and the accused, as well as everyone else assisting us. We have a witness scheduled for today, who we will be hearing in minute. But we have some housekeeping matters to deal with first of all. On the 11th of April, a written submission from the Defence was filed with us concerning the sixth version of the exhibit list. The documents referred to are voluminous. We have 284 exhibits referred to. To facilitate the Judges' work and the work of the Chamber's legal officers, as well as the work of the registrar, I would like to ask the Defence to provide us with a new list which contains only exhibits that have not yet been admitted, because in your submissions and the 284 pages, there are four categories of documents. There are some documents that have already been admitted, others that have been marked for identification, and then we have documents that have not yet been admitted into evidence. What I'm particularly interested in are the documents that have not yet been allocated exhibit numbers. In addition, in regard to these documents that do not yet have exhibit numbers, it would be useful to have in column number 11, since you have established columns, it would be good to have the name of the witness concerned in that column through whom the documents were shown or referred to. For example, document 352 which was used in the course of the testimony of the expert who was a witness in history. In column 11 there could be a reference to the witness's name. Similarly, it would also assist the Judges if we had another list, with this list in an alphabetical order. We could have the names of the witnesses in alphabetical order and by their names the numbers of the exhibits used in chronological order, the number of exhibits used. For example, in the came of witness Kasim Trnka, we could have this witness mentioned and then by the name of the witness reference to all the documents that were used when the witness testified. In the case of Trnka we might have 368, 372, et cetera. These documents could be referred to. In addition to these new lists, I'd like to point out that the Prosecution should inform us within two weeks of their position in relation to documents that have not been admitted so that we can render a written decision, which is what we did in the case of the Prosecution's exhibits, a written decision that concerns all these documents. Perhaps the Prosecution won't need two weeks, but let's say that we should have -- we should be informed of their position, of the Prosecution's position, as soon as possible. Having said that, there are two other issues I would like to deal with, issues that we had not dealt with yet with regard to translation, translation of P662. It concerns the term "odnosno." Mr. Registrar, we need a number for the memo dated the 27th of January, 2005, because we don't have a number for this memo. And we need to re-number three other memos that deal with the same issue which deal with the term "odnosno." The 27th of January, the 7th of February, and the 3rd of March are the dates of these memos. We need a common number with three tabs in chronological order. Mr. Registrar, if you have followed what I have said, you could perhaps inform us of these numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, in fact I was following you, and the registry suggests the following number: Under number C8 we would admit three different tab numbers. The first one refers to the first CLSS memo dated the 27th of January, 2005. Under tab number 2 we will have the CLSS memo dated the 7th of February, 2005. And finally, under tab 3 we'll have the memo dated the 3rd of March, 2005, the CLSS memo. This means that C8 which was allocated to the 7th of February memo shall be deleted and be replaced by the number I've mentioned. And C11, which concerns the 3rd of March memo, is also now redundant. So we have three different tabs under C8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The term "odnosno" has been examined by CLSS, and the memo is now under C8 and we have three tabs. We also have a problem that concerns DH165.6. We have a memo on the 22nd of February, 2004 that doesn't have a number. We have another memo dated the 14th of February, 2005, the number of which is C9. C9 should be a common number, and we should have two tabs under C9 in chronological order. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In accordance with your decision, C9 will have two tabs. The first one shall concern the CLSS memo dated the 22nd of February, 2004. And tab number 2 concerns CLSS memo dated the 14th of February, 2005. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And our last issue that we have to deal with -- and could the Prosecution please pay attention to what I will now say. With regard to the translation of the note from Witness ZP that concerns investigations that didn't bear any fruit. This note, and the Defence requested that it be admitted into evidence, well, we should rule on the Defence's request to have this document admitted into evidence. And before the registrar gives us with -- provides us with a number, the Prosecution should inform me of their position, unless the Prosecution requires some time to examine this issue that first arose quite a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we're referring I believe to the handwritten note dated the 20th of June, 2004, we have no objection to that being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As far as the written -- the handwritten note is concerned, could we have a number, Mr. Registrar? The 20th of June is the date. The interpreter made an error.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number will be DH2163/E for the note dated the 20th of June. [In English] This is the English translation. The original of this exhibit is admitted into evidence under the reference DH2163. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that Mr. Dixon is ready to get on his feet. Mr. Dixon, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. There's just one matter in relation to the translation issue for document C8, and that is that Your Honours will recall that we submitted an excerpt from the dictionary on the word "odnosno" explaining what the meaning of the word was, and Your Honours were given a copy of that and the Prosecution as well. And we would request, Your Honours, that that document also be made part of document C8, perhaps as tab number 4. It was a document that was referred to in the memoranda, the dictionary definition. If it would be part of all the documents, we would greatly appreciate that. Thank you. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, if you remember, the Defence provided a copy of an extract from a dictionary in Croatian and English, a Croatian and English dictionary, Zagreb 2001. And Defence counsel suggests that we give this document tab number 4 under C8. What would your position be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, with regard to this document could we have a tab number, please, since these are B/C/S terms translated into English. It would have been more complicated if the reverse had been the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In accordance with the Defence's request, this will be a document admitted into evidence under C8, and the tab number will be tab number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If there are any other versions, we could allocate other tab numbers, 5, 6, and 7, this will depend on versions, on the various versions that both parties might find. Perhaps the Prosecution will come across other translations of the term. This is why it's very useful to use tabs because we can continue adding other documents incessantly. If there are no other problems, Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good day, Madam Judge, good day, Your Honour. There are two issues I would like to raise. The first concerns a document that we should tender before the -- we should have tendered before the close of our case. This is a document that we have discussed and it has been shown to my colleagues from the Prosecution. It's a translation of the additional question that was put to the witness. Perhaps we can go into private session so I can mention the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With regard to the final exhibit lists and the comments to that list by the Prosecution, it was our earlier understanding that our two-week period would begin to run from the point in time when the Defence has notified us that all the translations in fact were available, and I'm wondering if we can perhaps have any additional information as to any remaining translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there are two possibilities. The 14-day time limit will start running as of the 11th of April, or as of the time when the last translation was provided. Could the Defence provide us with any information about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My colleague is right. In our written submission we suggested, and I think that an order has already been rendered by the Trial Chamber in this regard, we stated that the 14 days for the Prosecution would run as of the time the last translation has been filed. And I can now inform the Trial Chamber that we will file additional translations. We should be receiving them today, and we will file them on Thursday, Thursday, the 20th -- I apologise, the 21st of April. And then there will be one last filing which we will make on the 28th of April. And by that time we believe that we will have been provided with all the translations from the registry. This means that this would give the Prosecution up until the 12th of May to make any comments with regard to the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since that there will be two stages, the 12th of May would be a good date. Mr. Mundis, what's your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We anticipate no problems in meeting the deadline of the 12th of May. And of course we'll endeavour to respond sooner than that, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. If there are no other issues to deal with, we will now call the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President. While the witness is coming in, I believe the document that we've admitted that was dated the 20th of June, 2004, should be placed under seal, in light of the fact that the witness who provided that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was wondering about that. Mr. Registrar, with regard to the document dated the 21st of June, could we have the reference?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This document was in fact dated the 21st of June. It was under seal. I take note of the fact. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I would first of all like to check that technology is working. So could you let me know if you understand what I'm saying to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can hear you and I can understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Before taking an oath, I need to identify you. Could you give me your first name, your second name, your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Safet Junuzovic. I was born on the 12th of June, 1971, at a place called Kuka in the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do you have a job or a profession at the moment, and if so which one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I work for the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that leads me to conclude that you're a member of the armed forces. Can you tell me what your rank is at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. I'm a major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell me, with regard to the period 13 years ago, more than 13 years ago, 1992/1993, were you a member of the armed forces then and, if so, what unit were you a part of at the time and what rank did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In April 1992, I was in my second year of the military academy for ground forces in Belgrade. In July, I came to Bosnia and joined Municipal Staff of Territorial Defence of the city of Zenica. And I was a platoon commander in the 1st Zenica Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993 I was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and in April I am an operations officer within the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A commander, sir. Have you already testified before an international or a national tribunal with regard to facts that happened in your country in the period of time between 1992 and 1993, or is it the first time that you are testifying before justice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So far I've never testified, and this is the first time that I am before any court at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to read out the text of the oath that the usher is going to show you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Major, you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to General Kubura's Defence team, since they've asked you to appear as a Defence witness, so before I do that I'd like to give you some information, the same sort of information I give all witnesses with regard to the way in which we're going to be working here in the course of this hearing. You will first of all be called upon to answer questions which will be put to you by the Defence team. You will have met them previously in the course of the proofing for this hearing, and those questions are asked in such a way as to be neutral, and they will require you to provide answers which on occasion may be rather lengthy and elaborate. After that the Prosecution team, which is sitting to your right, through their representative, Mr. Mundis, will be asking you questions within the framework of what we tend to call in the common law procedure cross-examination. And within that framework, the questions that are going to be put to you may sometimes be leading questions. Following the cross-examination by the Prosecution team, the Defence team will be able to ask questions again. We should not forget General Hadzihasanovic's Defence team because they, too, before the Prosecution starts with their cross-examination, they too, as I was saying, will be able to put questions to you in case they deem that necessary for the purposes of their case. Once the Prosecution has completed their cross-examination, at that stage General Kubura's Defence team will be able to come back and ask you extra questions. Those extra questions, generally speaking, are also neutral questions without any leading questions being asked. Following this re-examination by the Defence team, General Hadzihasanovic's Defence team will also be able to ask you extra questions. The three Judges sitting in front of you will also be able to ask you questions at all times, but for reasons of convenience, as it were, we prefer to allow the Defence and the Prosecution to ask questions that they feel are most useful for the purposes of their cases. And in case we wish some more clarification with regard to any of your replies, we will indeed ask questions. And also if we feel that there are important gaps in the replies you will have given to these questions, we may try to fill those gaps by asking questions. Once we have asked our questions, we will leave it up to the Prosecution and the Defence to ask any other useful questions that they feel they wish to ask following the answers you have given to the Judges' questions. To the extent possible, please do and try reply in a concise and precise way to the questions asked because this is an oral procedure and this is why you can see in front of you the transcript, the translation into English of whatever said in this courtroom, and so this will be proof of what you say. It may well happen that in the course of the examination-in-chief or the cross-examination, the documents, which are almost all of military nature, may be shown to you, either because you yourself are the author of those documents or else because you may be familiar with them due to your previous duties. And at that stage you will be asked to comment on those documents and the types of those documents. I also need to draw your attention to two more important points. First of all, a very simple point, you've taken an oath stating that you will tell the truth, and that of course excludes the possibility of perjury. The second point is rather more complicated. It is included in our Rules of Procedure. If you are asked a question, you may refuse to answer the question if you believe that your reply may at some point in the future provide certain elements which might be used against you. In that case, you may well answer, No, I don't feel like answering that question. In that case, though, which has never happened so far, the Trial Chamber may nevertheless ask you to reply and guarantee that you have some sort of immunity. If in the course of our hearing today you feel that there are any problems, don't hesitate to let us know. For technical reasons and in order to be able to give you some rest between now and 7.00 p.m., we will have two breaks lasting between 20 and 30 minutes. As I've already mentioned, this is in order to give you some rest because you will no doubt see that answering questions nonstop is rather tiring, and also we, too, need these breaks in order to be able to change the tapes. Apart from that, if everything goes well you won't have to come back tomorrow, but that of course will depend on how much time will the Defence need in order to put the questions to you, and the same goes for the cross-examination by the Prosecution. Now I'd like to give the floor to the Defence team for General Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We'll try and make sure that we use our time in a rational manner so that we can complete this witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Junuzovic, we have heard you answer the question put to you by the Presiding Judge as to where you were in 1992 and 1993, so I'm not going to repeat that question once again. I would like to know when exactly it was when you joined the 7th Muslim Brigade and what exactly you did there.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of February I was ordered to join the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I was placed within the operations and training team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what order?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the order from the command, the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were a part of the operations and training body. Could you tell us what exactly was that about, what were your duties within that framework?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The operations and training body first and foremost has the duty to plan and to a certain extent participate in the implementation and carry out controls of training within units to which they belong; that's one aspect of our work. And the second aspect is the assessment of our own forces with regard to any operations they may be called upon to carry out and the planning of those operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When you joined the 7th Muslim Brigade, that is to say in February of 1993, who was the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Asim Koricic was the commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who was issuing orders to you at that time when you were working for the command of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: At that time the commander of the brigade, Asim Koricic, and then Amir Kubura was the Chief of Staff, and I myself mostly got my duties assigned to me by Ahmet Zubaca, who was an assistant to the Chief of Staff for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, could you tell us whether you know if at some point Mr. Koricic left the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when exactly it was, but it happened at some point in the beginning of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What was Mr. Kubura's position at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was less than clear, basically. He was not a deputy or a representative of the commander -- I mean when Mr. Koricic was leaving. So he was not an acting commander. He was not deputy or representative, and a whole range of issues came up, especially with regard to logistics and financial affairs of this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify what you mean by "less than clear"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: At that stage in our -- April 1994, there were instructions from the armed forces with regard to material and financial affairs and the bookkeeping. According to certain instructions and rules and regulations, the commanders of units were allowed to -- when it came to certain duties with regard to the reception and the dealing of financial matters or funds, they could ask other people to deal with it, either the deputy for logistics or the Chief of Staff or the assistants for financial affairs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question put by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up until the point when Mr. Koricic left the brigade, Amir Kubura used to sign this, but he said "on behalf for," so it would always read "Asim Koricic," and Mr. Kubura would sign on his behalf. So I think you will have seen a whole range of documents of this sort. And as far as I know, he was not officially given those duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What about the rules for the use of the seal?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: According to instructions with regard to office work, the commander and the Chief of Staff and his assistants, who were entitled to sign on his behalf or either on their own behalf, when it came to the general affairs office, they had to deposit their full signature there and their initials as well. So along with the seals. And it had to be indicated very clearly who was able to use the seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a slight mistake on the transcript on page 11. It should read "1993," but the transcript says "1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, could you tell us whether Mr. Kubura had an office within the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. It was situated within the staff premises. In one part of the building there was Mr. Kubura as the staff, and then his two assistants, one for operations and training, and the other for intelligence, together with experts, experts for intelligence, for operations and departments. And in the other part of the building, there was Mr. Asim Koricic with his assistants for logistics, financial affairs, and morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993 do you know exactly what office Mr. Kubura was using?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Until the very end of November or December, he used -- he used the offices of the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Koricic at some point came back to Zenica and to the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the beginning of September. The brigade at that time was on duty in the area of the municipality of Vitez. He came along. And if I may say so - and I mean this is my own opinion here - and everybody kept asking questions, how could he come, because all the roads were blocked. And then he asked openly about his own status, how come Amir Kubura all of a sudden was commander? And how was his status going to be solved? He inspected the units very often, especially the 1st Battalion, and he held a number of meetings there. But it basically created disarray at the time. At that stage I was the commander of the 1st Battalion, and it brought about a certain unease.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How long did he stay in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Up until mid-December he was in Bilmiste. And in mid-December he went to Travnik. He no longer appeared in Bilmiste, and I think that sometime in February some other unit had been established with its headquarters in Travnik, and he was at its head.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, at some time in 1993 did you become the commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of June, I went to Travnik. I left Zenica and went to Travnik. And the exact date when I was appointed as a commander was the 20th or the 21st of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You then arrived in Travnik and you became the commander of the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the period after the conflicts in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: According to the proposal from the brigade command, I was to take over the battalion in mid-April. But because the roads had been blocked and it was impossible to establish communications, this was postponed until it became possible to take over the battalion. This happened after the road from Zenica to Ovnak to Travnik had been opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What was the situation like in Travnik when you arrived in June 1993 and what was the situation like in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: At that period of time I saw that the battalion wasn't in just one place and didn't have just one task to carry out. I found a company in the zone of responsibility of the brigade in Bijelo Bucje in Travnik municipality. Part of the area faced Turbe, the other part Donji Vakuf. Part of the unit was engaged in the zone of responsibility of the 325th Vitez Brigade in the area of Poculica and Preocica. And a significant part of the troops were dispersed in various other units, including the 308th from Novi Travnik and then the brigade from Bugojno, rather, Vakuf that was in the area of Rostovo and Ravno Rostovo. And generally speaking the situation in the area was very difficult. Brigades had been established to a certain extent by that time, and they were holding lines facing the Chetnik aggressor on the plateau towards Vlasic and Vakuf, and in another area new lines were being established facing the HVO in the entire area of the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Travnik and assumed the duties of the brigade commander, did you have any meetings with officers from the Bosnian Krajina OG and with the commander?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: At the time in the battalion Mr. Terzic was in the battalion at the time. He was representing the brigade. He was there on behalf of the brigade. When I arrived in Travnik, when I took over the battalion, he took me to the command of the Bosnian Krajina OG. He introduced me to General Alagic at the time and to members of his command. I then met the commander of the 17th Krajina, Mr. Cuskic, and on the 18th or 19th, on the following day, there was a briefing attended by brigade commanders. And as I was -- or rather, as my battalion was the only one in Travnik and the other two battalions were in Zenica at the brigade command, I attended not on behalf of the 7th Muslim, but on behalf of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, when you arrived there, was part of the Bosnian Krajina OG?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The order on integrating the brigade within the Bosnian Krajina OG was issued earlier, in March I think. Since the zone of responsibility facing the Serbian aggressor was in that area that had been assigned to the Bosnian Krajina OG. And as a result, we were there up until the beginning of April in the zone of responsibility. We had forces the strength of a battalion there. And for that reason, during that period of time, the brigade was officially part of the Bosnian Krajina OG.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to use certain documents, and with your leave I would like to show these documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, when you arrived in Travnik were you informed where the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was engaged? I'm referring to combat activities at the beginning of June 1993 in the Travnik area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm only referring to troops the strength of a company. But at the time one platoon was in the zone of responsibility facing Bijelo Bucje, whereas the others - this included a company that lacked one platoon - part of the battalion command, communications department, and the police section, they were involved in combat together with the 17th Krajina. And I'm referring to engaging in action on the 8th and 9th in Hajdareve Njive and Sivica [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Hajdareve Njive?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a small pass -- or rather, it's not a pass, on the road between Travnik and Dolac in the direction of the Lasva Valley. There's a little hill there and that's where they were engaged in action there. That's between Travnik and Dolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How far is it from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not more than a kilometre and a half or two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the document under tab 4 in the bundle. It's a combat order from the Bosanska Krajina OG, dated the 9th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a new document. Mr. President. The Defence obtained it by examining archives of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So as not to waste any time, could you just have a look at the last sentence and read it out.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: "The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade with the 1st Battalion of the 17th Krajina Mountain Brigade are taking over Sibicara and Okuka."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: That order concerns the 9th of June, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where Sibicara and Okuka are located?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Sibicara is the name administrate match factory in the place called Dolac which is on the Travnik to Vitez road. And Okuka is the bridge that leads from that road to Dolac. It's to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How far is this area from Travnik and where is that exactly? How far is the Sibicara and Okuka area from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's at a distance of about three kilometres. It's on that road. It's on the road from Travnik to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When the witness was reading out, I think that something wasn't entered into the transcript. It doesn't say the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. That's when the witness was reading the last sentence in the document. I'm just saying that for the sake of the transcript. The witness could read out the sentence again or confirm that that is what he actually said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, from whom did you find out about the combat activities of the company? You said that they were involved in the area in Hajdareve Njive and Sibicara and Okuka? Who provided you with that information?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: My deputy Horo Naim and Jusovic Suad, the commander. They mentioned Hajdareve Njive because one of the platoon commanders was killed there, and they also mentioned someone called Zis who fought well and he was killed there. So that's why it's stuck in my memory and I know they were in Hajdareve Njive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain any information from the command of the Bosanska Krajina OG and from General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Not in relation to these events. This concerns activities they were involved in before I arrived there. I arrived ten days later. So I wasn't provided with any other information in the form of a document. This document was placed in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you say during which period you were the commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: From the 17th of June until the 9th of December, 1993. That's the exact period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: During that period while you were the commander of the 1st Battalion, did you receive an order of any kind to inform the command to Bosanska Krajina OG or the 3rd Corps of the participation of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade during this period from the beginning of June 1993? Were you asked to write a report of any kind?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was never asked to draft a report or an analysis or to do anything that related to those events and to the participation of those troops in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive an order of any kind requesting you -- asking you to submit a report on whether members of the 1st Battalion participated in combat in Maline at the beginning of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No. If we're talking about this company, they were only engaged in the Bijelo Bucje area and in the area of Hajdareve Njive and Sibicara.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Junuzovic, have you heard of the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I heard of the village of Miletici when an indictment was brought against Mr. Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I will now repeat the same question I put to you earlier on. When you were the commander did you receive an order of any kind asking you to report whether the 1st Battalion had ever been in Miletici and asking you to report on the events in the village of Miletici? Did you receive such an order from the commander of the Bosanska Krajina OG, from the security service, from your superior commander, or from the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: At that time and when I was one of the members of the brigade command in April and in May in Zenica and then later on as the battalion commander in Travnik, no one ever asked me about this and I never heard that someone in the brigade command had been asked about that village. And as I said, the first time I heard about that village was after an indictment had been brought. I didn't even know where this village was located. I have to have a look for the village by using a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now referring to the events in Maline, Bikosi, and Miletici. Was there any oral briefing concerning those events in the Bosanska Krajina OG?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Junuzovic, do you know that in the camp of Mehurici -- do you know that in the village of Mehurici there was a camp where foreign combatants stayed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever in that camp? Did you ever go to that camp?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from that camp come to the command of your battalion in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now have a look at the document in the bundle under tab 8. For the transcript it's document DH269. Have you had a look at the document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign the document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber how it is that you drafted this document.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: When preparing to carry out combat around the 24th of June in the of responsibility of the Bosanska Krajina OG and the Zapad OG, when preparing to carry out such combat there was a briefing with General Alagic. At that briefing, he orally put questions to us. He asked us whether we had men in that camp. He didn't only ask about my unit; he asked about all the other units, too. He wanted to know whether we had any of our men who were being trained there. He wanted to know whether any of our men had come from that camp. This was an oral request. In Bijelo Bucje and Ravno Rosto, the combat came to an end around the 24th or the 26th. The 7th Muslim Brigade went to the Visoko battlefield on the 1st of July. Here I'm referring to a document dated the 5th of July. Since there was no one in the battalion command who could use a signature or stamp - I'm referring to myself and my deputy - as a result, there was no reply to this document up until the 19th of July. And here I stated that we didn't have any such men. We didn't have men who had attended such training. And we didn't know what sort of units were concerned up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said "we have no right to command units in the Mehurici camp."

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On a number of occasions they insisted on knowing whether we had men up there, whether we had a unit or a squad up there, or whether we could command them, et cetera, et cetera. So it was quite clear that there was nothing we could do because they weren't part of our forces, they weren't under our command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said that General Alagic put this question to the other commanders.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Are those other commanders of brigades or units?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Other brigade commanders. And I believe that at the time they were the commanders of municipal staffs, too. The same question was put to them. Because of the connotations that camp had, there were young men, combatants who wanted to go there and train.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were they all at the same briefing that you attended with General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: There was the commander of the 17th Krajina, the commander of the 312th, I'm sure about them. The 306th wasn't present because they did not participate in those combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any foreigners while you were in Zenica, in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with them?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from meeting them in the street, on the roads, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When you met them in the street, did you ever talk to them?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, let's go back to the period of time when you were at the command of the brigade. Did you as member of the command in the beginning of June participate in any combat operations that the 7th Muslim Brigade participated in in the area of Ovnak mountain pass?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Within the framework of the brigade command, I was at the forward command post in the village of Vrselje, and if you consider that to be active participation, in that case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at the documents marked 1, 2, and 3 in this folder. 1 is a new one, and numbers 2 are P420 and 419. Do you know the document number 1?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what it means with reference to this date, the 5th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This is a question which was created on the 4th of June. It was drafted at the operations and training body, and I am the author of the document; I drafted it. And on behalf of commander, we have the signature by Amir Kubura. It is reconnaissance -- command reconnaissance plan for the 5th of June. There is an explanation of what group is going to carry out that reconnaissance mission and the description of their work and their tasks in the two main points in the illustration here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the next document, number P420. It's number 2 in your folder. Could you take a look at item 2, please. What units participated in these activities in this area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In number 1 it is indicated that three detachments of the 7th Muslim Brigade were going to participate. So it's the complete 2nd Battalion, which at that stage consisted of two detachments. And there was participation of the 3rd Battalion, which was made up of one detachment at the time. And then the 314th Motorised Brigade from Zenica, the company from the manoeuvring detachment, that is to say MUP, and the company from the second part of the defence of Zenica, and the brigade group from the 314th Motorised Brigade. It is a command of the tactics group and the units of that group. It was a formation which was set up temporarily for the purposes of the carrying out of that task only.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to use a map with this witness. So if you would allow me, we would like to submit the map now -- we would like to show the map to the witness in order to clarify these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, could you take a felt-tipped pen, and if you can, could you please mark on this map where exactly the 7th Muslim Brigade was active in the course of these combat activities for defence purposes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: According to the order issued by the commander of the tactical group, the main forces were made up of the units of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and they had the task of going from Porice [phoen] and Vrselje and to take the forces to the sector called Crni Vrh, which is this part over here. Crni Vrh was the starting position for attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Just in order to make it easier for us, could you put number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. And their next task was to attack in the area of Usice and Novo Selo. That was a task assigned to the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What you marked right now at the very end --

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The arrow marks the section -- the sector of Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you draw a circle there and mark it properly.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. The second anti-sabotage detachment with manoeuvre company with an attack from the direction of Konjevici in the direction of Grahovcici. And members of the 314th with the municipal defence staff were attacking Crnjac from sector of Krnjaki [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when exactly these activities started in this sector.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: They had been planned for the 7th of June, presumably, but due to certain errors in communications and the fact that we could not prepare the positions on time, we were not prepared, and so we delayed it until the 8th. And in the morning of the 8th, the battalion carried out the task successfully so that by noon we arrived at Ovnak.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So just to clarify, this is the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the 3rd Battalion at that time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion was a reserve battalion for the 2nd Battalion. Basically to a certain extent they were involved in combat activities, but only once fighting started in the sector of Novo Selo itself, when fighting broke out in town, house to house basically. Up until that time there was no need for them to be involved, for the 3rd Battalion to be involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On a number of occasions I mentioned Ovnak and you did, too, in your answers. What is Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Ovnak is a mountain pass on the road from Zenica to Nova Han Bila in the direction of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it a village? Is it inhabited?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at it on the map?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, on the basis of my experience of map reading, Ovnak is only shown as a mountain pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the document which is marked number 14 in your folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's a new document that the Defence got from the federal statistics office in Sarajevo. And we would like to determine what exactly Ovnak is and can the answer be based on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just read out the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: "We are informing you on the basis of your request that an inhabited settlement, Ovnak, does not exist either in the territory of the municipality of Zenica or Travnik."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether this could be the right time for a break since it's 3.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. We shall have a break now and we'll start again at five minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can resume. The Defence team has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, could you tell the Trial Chamber whether members of the 2nd and the 3rd Battalion when it came to these combat activities ever entered the village of Brajkovici.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to put the same question with regard to the village Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the 2nd and the 3rd Battalion, if you think in terms of the entire formation, did not, except for some reconnaissance platoons who had to be in front of their battalions in terms of combat security.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What about the village of Susanj?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Susanj was complete deserted and it was not included in any sort of combat activity. So it had not been planned for the units either to go through there nor did any units receive any tasks there. There was some threats, but they thought that maybe they should check out whether there were any enemy soldiers there, but basically for all intents and purposes the village was deserted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You did say in the course of your testimony that these combat activities were completed on the 8th of June, in the afternoon of the 8th of June, if my understanding is correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: They were completed in the sector of Novo Selo, that is to say, the mountain pass Ovnak -- I mean, I know this myself. I saw the commanders of the 2nd and the 3rd Battalion there at noon, and we did not go any further. So it was around noon. And individual combat operations continued until early afternoon, no later than 4.00 p.m., and I think there were a couple of snipers there. And there was a bunker at the end of Novo Selo, and combat operations for these two or three buildings continued for a couple of hours more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: After the end of combat activities, if all that was over in the afternoon, that is to say 4.00 p.m., what happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the brigade command received the order to move in the direction of Kakanj, and they were told that they should start engaging in combat activity in the municipality of Kakanj. In order to do that, I myself and a number of commanders from the staff left that afternoon. First of all we went to Zenica, and afterwards we went to Kakanj, and we were received by the then member of the operations group Istok, Mr. Nehru Ganic, and that was when night fell more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I need to interrupt you. When exactly did you leave the area of Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who else went to Kakanj with you on that day?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I do know that apart from the driver and one escort I had the chief of ABiH services, Ibrahimagic Edin, and the artillery chief Durmis, I think, and the commander of the reconnaissance company of the brigade, and a part of the logistics staff as well, some officers from logistics. On the 9th of June we were at Kakanj. On the 9th of June I went back to Zenica with those same officers to get the necessary documents for the upcoming combat activities. I do know that some parts of brigades -- of the brigade of Ovnak certainly left the area in the afternoon of the 9th of June. When I say "parts," what I mean was those who were behind, the logistics, the anti-aircraft defence liaison, anything that had to do with a lot of technological and technical support, they had all left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When exactly, for what period did the members of the 2nd and 3rd stay in Ovnak and then when did they leave, and did they go to Zenica or Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In that area, in that area of Ovnak, the brigade did not stay after the afternoon hours of the 9th of June. It was for the following reasons. The units had to rest and they had to prepare for Kakanj, and they first of all had to organise and carry out the transport operation to Kakanj. And our aim of all this was to organise transport to Kakanj and not even to reach the outskirts of the city itself. The units were not supposed to enter the city or enter the sector of the railway station, which is at the very entrance to the city or the bus station which is there as well. Our aim was to imperceptibly bring our forces to the area of Kakanj. If you want to achieve that sort of effect, it requires a great deal of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could we clarify that. You said that the members of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion arrived to that area on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: They arrived on the 6th, in the late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And they left on the 9th of June?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No later than the afternoon of the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier on that the chief of artillery, Durmis went with you to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Durmis, Ibrahim. Mr. Junuzovic, in that period of time when the members of the 7th Brigade were in that area, did you hear about any looting or destruction of any property? I would like you to take a look at the document number 7 in your folder.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at item 4 and comment on this report. It was sent to the 3rd Corps command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I'll first read through it and then I will provide you with your -- with my answer. "Individual cases of burning and destruction of property in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade zone of responsibility did occur after the combat operations, but after the end of combat operations the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade were transferred from the region of Ovnak to the region of Zagradje Kakanj. So any destruction after that end of combat operations cannot be the responsibility of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade." In response to one of your questions, I have already said that there was fighting that went on until the late afternoon because a few snipers remained there and, I know that there was also a machine-gun nest. Naturally, when you have such fighting in inhabited places, there are ricochets, sporadic shooting, and properties are inevitably damages, houses and roofs. There was such damage, that's for sure, and there was such damage on both sides. After we left, naturally we couldn't assume responsibility. We were responsible if there was any -- for buildings that had been set on fire or damaged after we left. But since I lived in the municipality of Zenica in the settlement called Police which is on the old road from Zenica to Sarajevo, that is on the left bank of the Bosna River. There are three settlements near my settlement, and up until the summer of 1993 the majority of the population in those settlements was Serbian. They left in May, April, or June, when I wasn't in Zenica. On the 5th of July I arrived in Zenica -- and what am I trying to say? Well, in November the town of Jajce fell, and 70 or 80 per cent of the refugees from there arrived in Zenica municipality. The municipal Territorial Defence Staff and the municipal authorities tried to find accommodation for these people in abandoned Serbian houses. But I know that there were individual cases of looting. For example, roofs were looted, or rather the tiles, and carpentry in those houses. These are Bosnians who were in those places. There was probably looting in the sector of Ovnak. And this occurred in November. It was raining at the time already. It wasn't summer, so you couldn't just cover the windows with a sheet of nylon, a sheet of plastic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 34, line 19, when I --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is what I colleague is going to say now. That if he doesn't say that, I will intervene because there was some confusion as far as the question and answer is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 34, line 13, when I asked the witness whether he was familiar with the name of the chief of the artillery of the 7th Muslim Brigade, since earlier on the surname Durmis had been mentioned, the witness said that his name was Ibrahim.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to make sure that the transcript is quite precise, my colleague has just said that he asked the witness a question. He asked him whether he knew his name; that's page 34, line 16. But this question that the lawyer put to the witness was not entered into the transcript. And then in line 18 the witness first said "I cannot remember." That was entered into the transcript. And then he entered Durmis, Ibrahim. This part of the witness's answer was erroneously entered on line 19 as a new question put by Defence counsel. That's not the question; that's not where the question started. The question started at line 20. So in order to be quite clear, and in order to distinguish between the question and the answer, I think that it was necessary to correct this part of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To make sure that everything is clear, I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the chief of the artillery of the 7th Muslim Brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: His name is Ibrahim and his last name is Durmis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, since you said that the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade had started leaving the sector on the 9th of June, could you have a look at the documents in the bundle of documents. Could you have a look at the documents under tab number 5 and under tab number 6. And could you first tell us whether you recognise these documents and who drafted them.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This is a commander's reconnaissance plan for the 10th. I drafted the document, but someone else signed on my behalf. But this is my handwriting. It was authorised by the Chief of Staff. It concerns carry out reconnaissance of new operation zones. In one item reference is made to the composition of the groups that will be involved in reconnaissance, and it also refers to their tasks and the time that they will spend on carrying out these tasks. It concerns the area of Kakanj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, this is DK23 [realtime transcript read in error "DK34"].

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me when this document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It was drafted on the 9th, in the evening. It was drafted in the evening hours after midnight. The Chief of Staff, Amir Kubura, signed it between 7.00 and 8.00. How is it that I know this? Because I went home at 6.00 to deal with certain private matters, so the documents that had been prepared and that related to reconnaissance, the documents that I left with the other operations officers, and their task was to have Amir Kubura sign them and to have these activities carried out on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the left upper-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I approve, I approve the Chief of Staff, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel, in line 1, page 34, there's a reference to DK34. Wasn't there a mistake? Is that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The document concerned is DK23. It must have been mistakenly recorded, erroneously recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kubura signed as Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade here on the 10th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a brief look at the following document, DK24. Do you recognise this document and what sort of a document is it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This is an order for an attack from the command of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. This order was issued. In the left-hand corner it says when it was issued, or rather when it was forwarded to the battalion commanders. It was at 1000 hours on the 11th of June, 1993. It says: "Be ready to attack by 1000 hours on the 12th."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This document DK24 refers to an order, is an order, an order to attack in the Kakanj area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Does this concern the period that you mentioned when the 7th Muslim Brigade left the Ovnak sector?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the last page of this document. Who signed the document and how did Mr. Kubura sign?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff, Amir Kubura, signed it as the Chief of Staff, not as the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like to move on to another subject now, but first of all I have two questions that relate to the time that the witness was the brigade commander. I would like to repeat one question because on page 17, line 16, the answer was perhaps unclear. My question to the witness concerned the time when Mr. Koricic left the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When he left the brigade, who signed the brigade documents and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The documents were signed by Amir Kubura in the capacity of Chief of Staff. Most of the documents refer to the commander Asim Koricic. There are individual documents where reference is made to the Chief of Staff, Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I have one more question that wasn't put to the witness -- that hasn't been put to the witness yet. When you were in the brigade command and you had the role that you already mentioned, did you attend briefings in the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: After Ahmet Zubaca went to Travnik, after the 16th of March, yes, I did attend those briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At those briefings, was the subject of the music school ever raised?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not at the time nor when I was the battalion commander. The music school was frequently mentioned in counts in the indictment and elsewhere. Mr. Talic Nesib who was then the assistant commander for security never mentioned that there had been problems in the music school. With regard to the music school, I'll provide you with an example. At some time in summer 1993, a member of my battalion was detained in that music school because he was inebriated. The men in that music school didn't allow me to visit that man as the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Junuzovic, I would now like to move on to another subject. At the beginning of November 1993, were you in the town of Vares and did you participate in the combat around the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What duties did you perform at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the 2nd Battalion -- of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we would like to use a map in relation to this subject, again I don't think it will take long, with your leave, I would like to show this map to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, could you first tell us on the 4th of November, 1993, were you in Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber how it is that you or your members from the 1st Battalion were before Vares or in the town Vares itself?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, initially the plan was that the brigade should start engaging in combat on the 3rd, but since there were transport difficulties, we didn't have fuel to transport the brigades, we didn't have fuel for jeeps, lorries, and for the other vehicles that we had. Given these problems, it was not until the 3rd in the early morning that the brigade command managed to obtain some diesel fuel for a diesel locomotive. So the entire brigade - the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalion - was transferred, was taken to this place -- you can't see it in the map. It's settlement near the town of Visoko. As they were taken there by train. Afterwards -- well, there were buses waiting for us in Visoko, and we were driven to the village of Malo Cajno. According to the plan these buses were to take us as far as the village of Strijezevo. I'll point to its location here. We had been taken to the Malo Cajno sector, and the plan was to be taken to the village of Strijezevo by bus. But because there was shelling, because Malo Cajno and this part here were being shelled, part of the brigade managed to get through to Strijezevo and the other part didn't manage to reach that point, so most of the men from the brigade arrived there on foot.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear Defence counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How far is Cajno from Strijezevo?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: If you take the forest path, if you have a look at the pass marked here, it's between 20 and 25 kilometres away, but the guides that we had been assigned got us there in three to four hours. It was late in the afternoon on the 3rd that we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the location of the villages of Cajno and Strijezevo on this map. Could you do so with the felt-tip, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And could you mark the village of Cajno with number 1 and mark the other location with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What's the distance between these two villages, just to make sure that everything is clear?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: According to the map, 25 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did your battalion go there on foot?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my battalion did, but I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What happened upon arriving in the village of Strijezevo?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since we arrived there in the late afternoon we heard that a plan -- there was a plan for an operation that the 7th had to carry out. Units of the municipal staff from the Vares municipality had carried out that task to a certain extent. So we didn't comply with the plan that had been issued, not completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at document under tab number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, this is a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the order for attack that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but there had been a change. It was a matter of using my battalion in the main line of attack. So this is according to the document that we have in front of us, but it did not happen that way because some fighters who were within the 2nd Battalion were from the municipality of Vares. I don't know, they were either born or living there, so it was decided that this same task, somewhat modified -- well, the order did not include the already -- the lines already taken by the units I had mentioned before. So there were the following changes: The 2nd Battalion was interested with the task in relation to entering the city of Vares to the left with regard to the road from Breza. I'm going to mark it by 3. What I mean is the 2nd Battalion. The 3rd Battalion was interested with the task of going from the sector of Budozelji to the city of Vares. I myself with my battalion was reserve battalion and I was in this sector. In the sector called Pajtov Han.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any combat operations in the city itself or around the city?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The entire time after we received orders to move on and carry out that task, I was talking about Thursday here, the 4th, since it was a relatively unknown terrain, and I especially mean from the point of view of my own battalion, the 3rd one, and it was raining and there was a lot of fog in the morning, and we could only move very slowly. Because we did not know where exactly the enemy lines were, whether there were any enemy lines there. We only found out later that there were none. And especially in those mountain and wooded areas. At some point in the morning, at around 8.00, the 2nd and the 3rd Battalion and the reconnaissance platoon from my battalion met, entering Vares at Majdan, and us, the three battalion commanders met there. So by 10.00 a.m., all three of us got there. The 3rd Battalion found it a bit more difficult to make progress because they had to go through the villages of Mir and Stupni Do. Prior to that, in the month of October, a massacre was perpetrated against the Bosniak population in that area, and it was believed by then the UNPROFOR forces had taken out all the survivors as well as all the dead bodies. But we heard that they came across a couple of more dead bodies in that area, and so they started to do some work there. And the 3rd Battalion also found it difficult because they had constant threats and the possibility of being attacked by the Serb aggressors, by Chetniks. And the 2nd Battalion found it very difficult to move ahead because they were going through dense forests. I was in Pajtov Han, and MUP was in charge of the checkpoint there. And the entire battalion was redistributed over an area of a couple of kilometres. So we started the whole operation at some point at around 4.00 p.m., and by 8.00, the first units, the reconnaissance detachments, got to Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you this question earlier on. Was there any combat activity at the entrance to the city or within the city?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were no major battles. The battalions did not fight enemy formations as such, but there was fighting with regard to snipers and other such elements. What I mean is this sort of fighting. Upon entering the city, it was still rather foggy. And you couldn't see very far, perhaps five to 600 metres. And afterwards later on, at around 10.00, when it became light, we noticed that a couple of buildings, afterwards it turned out it was just one building which had been set alight, but it was not set alight due to combat activities. And I suppose -- well, there was nobody else in front of us at least in as far as the direction from Breza is concerned, there were no other formations there. And the MUP officers entered the city at the same time. I mean it could have been proven by the fact -- well, we were told, no, no, no, let's stop, and we don't know what's going to happen there. And then they said, no, the city has been deserted and we want to set free the people who had been imprisoned in the primary school. And then we could see their comings and goings in their vehicles. But there was no major combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself enter Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I did not go any further than Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us exactly where it is, Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody else enter Vares Majdan with you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure of the commander about the 2nd battalion. As to the commander of the 3rd Battalion he had some problems because battle was still ongoing and possibility of movement -- look, Vares is a town which is in a valley and it has one main street which is relatively flat, but it's open and visible.
