And there's always possibility of snipers or some other type of attack from the right-hand side which is not inhabited and there are forests there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did members of your battalion, those who were there, enter there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Only my reconnaissance platoon was with me because there was no need for anyone else, because according to my orders I was not asked to bring any more forces because we were in reserve. And alongside the 2nd and the 3rd Battalion, well, basically I was two kilometres behind them. So there was myself and several members of my command, and there was this reconnaissance platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: How many soldiers are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No more than 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You and the members of your reconnaissance platoon, how long did you stay at Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No longer than late afternoon. The situation was as follows, and I'm talking about my own battalion right now: On that afternoon I was asked to the forward command post in Zvijezda. It was an urgent call and I was given a new task there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. But you stayed in the town of Vares only several hours as far as I could gather?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And there was a lot of police and a lot of UNPROFOR forces in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, page 46, line 20, should read Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In that period of time when you were at Vares Majdan, the members of this reconnaissance platoon, did they notice any destruction of any buildings or any lootings carried out by members of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Not with regard to members of my battalions. When I give you the following answer what I have in mind is this: We didn't notice when we came in that that building was on fire. It was a kilometre or a kilometre and a half away from us. I had a very small formation, very few men, and I could keep them under control and I could check exactly what everyone was doing. But as time was passing on that day, 10.00, 11.00, 12.00, other soldiers came along. In the last analysis there was the general population as well. That period of time is well-known for being a period of famine in Central Bosnia, especially in Breza, Zenica, Vares. I myself on that day did see civilians carrying a sack of flour, for example, and civilian police could do nothing about it. They would say, Okay, you can kill me but I'm taking this sack of flour back home because my family is going hungry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a checkpoint entering Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who was in charge of it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: That checkpoint from part of Han had been moved to Vares Majdan. MUP forces did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did they check the comings and goings?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier on you started talking about how you were assigned a new task in the afternoon, so I would like to answer that question now. And in order to make things easier, could you take a look at document number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, this is a new document, Mr. Chairman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is an order to attack, referring to my battalion only. I was given orders orally late at night at around 9.00 p.m. on the 4th at the village of Strijezevo, and it is about the use of my battalion in the direction of Dastansko. It is about a task, the goal of which it was to prevent surrendering that area that was between the HVO forces and the Serb aggressors, because that would mean that the city of Vares and its destiny would be put into question, and therefore the connections and the road across the mountain of Zvijezda and direction of Tuzla, there would be a real danger for that road to be blocked off. And that area of broader Tuzla would be basically be isolated with no communications at all. And so I was given those orders with that goal. And so on the 5th of April, at around 4.00 or 5.00 I took my entire battalion to our own sector of origin. And in the morning of the 5th between 8.00 and 10.00 we made preparations with regard to this task within the battalion. And at 10.00 we went from Strijezevo by bus in the direction of Bijelo Borje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This order to attack, is it with regard to the 5th of November?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 5th of November. The preparedness was achieved at 2.00 p.m. At five minutes to 2.00, I was told to stop any activities whatsoever. Since I suspected that it did not come from the Chief of Staff, Amir Kubura, I asked for a coded confirmation to suspend our operations. After about five to ten minutes, I got that, it had been confirmed, and I also got a message according to which the units of the 2nd Corps were to carry out that task. Let me just add at this stage, with regard to the question you asked earlier on and the answer I gave to you earlier on as to why we did not enter Vares. Because of fog. Because there was this real danger of a conflict amongst our own units. Because from the mountain of Zvijezda there were units of the 2nd Corps coming from the direction of Vares, so there was no need for us to go any further than Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Since this order to attack was with regard to the 5th of November, let me ask you whether you or the members of the 1st Battalion entered Vares at all?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No. We could not enter Vares at all because we had a very short period of time available, and I only had that day available in which to carry out the task, the combat task I had been assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like to the witness to be shown another map. This is a map we obtained by going Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. through the army archives. We have already talked to our colleagues from the Prosecution with regard to the use of that map, and they did not have any comments. And this is with regard to the 5th of November, 1993, and the way in which this battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Who drew it up?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The then-assistant of the Chief of Staff for operations and training, Saban Zunic. This is his signature. Vares on the 4th of November, that's when it was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Does this map illustrate the activities or possible combat activities that should have taken place on the 5th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: According to this map, the task of your battalion would have been to engage in combat activity in the sector of the village of Dastansko?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show this on the map? Don't mark this because it belongs to the archives. This is the original and we will be tendering it later on. Just a couple more questions, Mr. Junuzovic. After the 5th of November what happened then? When did your battalion leave this sector and where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Late in the afternoon on the 5th we went to our own sector of origin and the battalion went back on the 6th. On the 6th, in the morning, we left the sector of the village of Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In the same way we came. At that stage there was already a possibility to travel by bus all the way to Visoko. And then from Visoko we took the train to Zenica. And on that day, the 6th in the afternoon, people for the first time were asked to go on leave by -- on foot because there was no transport organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this concludes the examination-in-chief. I have no further questions. As to maps that were shown to the witness, perhaps after the cross-examination the witness could sign them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine then. Usher, could you please go and get the map so I can take a look at it. No, not that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does General Hadzihasanovic's defence have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We do have several questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Junuzovic, in replying to questions of my learned friend you said, if I may put it this way, that you were a participant in the battles at the mountain pass of Ovnak in June 1993. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Junuzovic, since previously as well as you could show us in a document you were involved in some reconnaissance, is it correct that HVO prior to that, since the month of May, had powerful strongholds in that area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. When I mentioned that we had certain problems in carrying out these operations, that is to say, combat activities should have started for that tactical group that had been set up, they were supposed to start on the 7th, but to a certain extent they had been suspended due to problems with regard to liaison and artillery support. And when it comes to the artillery support, what I mean is our inability to neutralise their positions. Any attempt to start carrying out these operations -- well, we did try on the 7th, but we encountered a great deal of resistance. We thought that it would be a rather easy task, but then it had to be postponed until the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also in answering another question put to you by my colleague you said that when you reached Novo Selo, only then the company of the 3rd Battalion joined you, since you then practically started house-to-house fighting in town. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Junuzovic, that when entering and starting this house-to-house fighting, as you called it, that you basically encountered the fact that almost in every house there were members of the HVO forces, armed members of those forces, and that you had to fight from house to house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me put to you another question. I would like to clarify a couple of issues in relation to the previous questions asked by my colleague, and it has to do with your arrival to Travnik on the 17th of June. You said that when you arrived you first wanted to check out the situation within your battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were faced with a situation in which parts of your own battalion due to the blockade by the HVO in the preceding period were scattered around in different places. You mentioned Poculica they were under the command of the 325th and so on and so forth. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, in conjunction with that did you have a full overview of the general combat situation in that area, the area in which there were parts of your battalion? Were you able to see yourself how they found themselves in, for example the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As to this brigade, I know they were in a very difficult position indeed, because every time I went to Travnik or I went from Travnik to Zenica I had to go through their area of responsibility, and the newly established lines in the direction of the HVO were in that area. What I mean in first place is the section -- the sector of the village of Mosor and to a certain extent the village of Alihodze. These two places in particular I know about because I travelled through them on my way to Travnik. And I do know they had difficulties with that front line at Vlasic because earlier I had been a member of the 314th, and on one occasion I was involved in work at the defence lines, and my neighbour basically to the left was the 306th Brigade. And after I took over this battalion I often met and encountered the members of the 306th Brigade, and I do know that they found themselves in a very difficult situation indeed. Basically it was a brigade which was set up in that -- it included the inhabitants of the villages in the areas, and I know that they had problems with communications. There was only one telephone line at the brigade command, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that by the end of April you should have gone to Travnik, but due to this blockade such a proposition could not go ahead. Up until the point in time when there was a proper link between Zenica and Travnik. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, once these communications had been established and as a commander of the battalion which in that area also had some members, in the course of that period of time did you see the large-scale movements of the population which due to this blockade, this isolation, was moving between Travnik and Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to quote one example here. This matter of food -- flour, basically. Was kind of critical and there was some promises or indications that there might be some flour at Bugojno. And quite a number of people from Zenica, from Mehurici, and this whole group of villages in the valley of Bila and Travnik set off to look for it either on foot or on tractors, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Considering this overall blockade and arms embargo, what about this matter of weapons and shortage of ammunition? Was it something that most commanders were particularly worried about in this period in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We kept wondering about how we could do anything if we only had 5, 10, 15 bullets in a weapon or if, as was our case in the 3rd Battalion where in the summer of 1993 there were about 500 fighters there, and only about 20 or -- 200, sorry, and 220 weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at this document that you have in front of you, number 4, and I'm going to ask you one more question and this will conclude my counter -- my cross-examination. This is a document which is basically an order, amongst other things, an order directed at the 1st Battalion of the 7th Brigade, even in the period before you joined it you became familiar with this only after your arrival to Travnik. But since you were a student at the military academy and later on as the commander you participated in this war, can you agree with me if I say that at the bottom of the page where it says: "Commencing of artillery support at 4.20 hours and commencing of attack at 4.30" that this in fact represents something which is far below the minimum level of artillery support for the activity of any battalion, that is to say, the minimum time is half an hour of artillery support, and what we have here, what is indicated here is just 10 minutes. And this is precisely the result of the inability for you to have any more than that because you did not have any artillery to speak of. Can you agree?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the command of the OG Bosanska Krajina did not really, apart from my company because we had about a hundred, they took three battalions from the 17th Krajina, and it is about the size of a brigade. And the minimum amount of time for preparations for a brigade is about 30 minutes. And on average they would have to shoot at least twice from every weapon. What he mentioned here, he said the combined artillery division, but it never went beyond 90 per cent [as interpreted] of all the means we had. So this is the bare minimum.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And does it confirm what you said, that you had no weapons to speak of in order to engage in this sort of combat activity?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The artillery preparation of any company I think would have to be longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take another look at this. The first indent where it says the 1st Company --

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No, the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 1st Battalion of the 17th Krajina Battalion -- or rather Brigade. Says that the 107-millimetre mortar would be used and 10 shells would be used. Can you agree with me that if I say that the normal use of this weapon in this sort of situation would mean 1.500 rockets and that 15 rockets is next to nothing?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm first of all going to answer to your question about mortars. It says that they have got ten mines and that ten mines are being approved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. On page 55, line 22 -- 23, rather, you said that it was 50 per cent, and in this transcript it says 90 per cent. So I would just like to have this corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please continue. I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The usual combat set for 120-millimetre mortar consists of 34 shells. So this means this is a third. I'm speaking about one mortar. And as far as the 107-millimetre launcher is concerned, yes, that's also a minimum. You don't go below this number. And in fact if you use 15 rockets, that no longer has any sort of effect because you're using the forces of one brigade, three battalions, and more, and if you use 15 rockets, well -- and ten shells, well, you can do that in ten minutes. And what do you do for the rest of the day? If you engage your forces there will be no possibility of providing them with support.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My last question is: This document that you've just been shown quite clearly shows the type of equipment that army units had. This is quite clearly referred to in the document dated the 9th of June, 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Junuzovic. My name is Daryl Mundis, and along with my colleagues here we represent the Prosecution in this case. I have just a few questions for you, sir. But let me start with this document that my learned colleague from the Hadzihasanovic Defence just showed you. I understand, sir, when you're talking about 107-millimetre launcher and 15 rockets having no effect, you're talking about in terms of standard military use of that weapons system. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Because certainly if you were on the receiving end of 15 rockets having been launched from 107-millimetre launcher, whether it was one rocket coming in at you, or two, or seven, or nine, or 12, that very well might have an effect on you as an infantry soldier, on the receiving end?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily. And when I say "not necessarily," I say so because these shells and these rockets weren't standard types. And sometimes their effectiveness was diminished 100 per cent. They were made in makeshift workshops, in factories where the men had no experience. Because this is equipment used in 1993. The last time that standard equipment was produced in the central Bosnian area was in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn, sir, to the campaign to liberate, for lack of a better term, Vares. In early November when your battalion was in Vares Majdan, can you tell us where the commander of the 7th Mountain Brigade, Amir Kubura, was physically located?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Which day? Which date are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let's start with to the best of your knowledge and recollection --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't have an objection, just a technical comment. I'd just like to ask the witness not to make any markings on the original map. There are the two other maps that he could mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But with the pointer he could indicate the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if we could just start with at the time the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade commander, Amir Kubura, arrived in the immediate vicinity of Vares, can you tell us the approximate date and time and the location where he was to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd in the evening he was in the village of Strijezevo, on the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, did you as a battalion commander, the commander of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, did you meet with the brigade commander, Amir Kubura, on the evening of the 3rd in Strijezevo?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were the other battalion commanders also present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Following that meeting on the 3rd of November, when was the next time you saw the brigade commander and where?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 4th in the same building in the same village. I was issued a task that had to do -- carry out combat activities planned for the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on that occasion, sir, on the 4th, when you saw and spoke with the brigade commander, did you see him at any other point on that day?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him in the late afternoon on that day, when I arrived in Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you met with him in the morning and then you saw him again in the late afternoon. Did you see him at any other point on the 4th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How about on the 5th of November, 1993, did you see the brigade commander, Amir Kubura, on that day, and if so where?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him on that day. If you exclude the afternoon when I arrived in the village of Strijezevo. But I do know that in the Vares Majdan sector he had a meeting with the chief of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us how far approximately Vares Majdan is from the centre of the town of Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Two to three kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you were leaving Vares and heading south along the road, you would pass through Vares Majdan?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On the 6th of November, 1993, did you have any meetings with the brigade commander, Amir Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that I met on the 6th, but only in the evening hours in Zenica. I don't remember having seen him on the 6th in the morning, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So when you say "on the 6th [realtime transcript read in error "4th"] of November in Zenica," would that be back at the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, about the discussions that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a mistake on page 60, line 11, of the transcript when my colleague asked a question it concerned the 6th of November, not the 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I was in fact talking about the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, sir, when you say that you met with the brigade commander on the 6th in Zenica, you were in fact referring to the 6th of November, 1993 at the headquarters of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us on those occasions when you met with the brigade commander prior to units of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade entering the immediate vicinity of Vares, including Vares Majdan, what were you discussing? Did those discussions concern combat plans and orders and operations and how those operations were to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Vares operation is concerned, the situation between the brigade commander and battalion commanders was confused. Why? For the following reasons: We had planned to carry out the operation in one way, and we hadn't planned to enter the town. However, the Vares municipal staff probably decided independently and part of the Kakanj municipal staff units also probably took an independent decision. And the lines that had been established up until then, they believed that they could carry this out on their own. They started doing this on the 3rd. So our problem was how to continue with our operation. And naturally, on the 3rd we discussed how to carry out the entire operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect, sir, to the units, whether they were brigades or companies of brigades, of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, who issued the orders with respect to the campaign concerning Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: A starting point had been assigned in the order issued. The 2nd Battalion practically took over my role and they advanced on the left side. But in that morning, no one thought it was necessary to issue orders of any kind. We just followed the order that related to changing the lines reached, and that's what the units did that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I don't believe, sir, that my question was clear, but you've mentioned the Vares municipal staff and the Kakanj municipal staff units. Let me ask you the same question in a slightly different way. The 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, were they receiving orders from the brigade commander, Amir Kubura, or were they receiving orders from either the Vares municipal staff or the Kakanj municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: From the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So throughout the time period, sir, that your battalion was in the area Vares, you were receiving orders from the brigade commander, Amir Kubura. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you were reporting back on activities of your battalion to Amir Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you recall at any point in time after or during the withdrawal from Vares whether the subject of looting was discussed with the brigade commander, and I'm talking about looting concerning soldiers of any unit of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I don't understand the part in which you asked me whether someone spoke to him. You have to ask me about a particular person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'd like to know at any meeting of the brigade command while you and the other battalion commanders and the brigade commander and the brigade staff were still present in the area of Vares in the first few days -- first six, seven days of November 1993, whether you were ever present at any meeting in which the subject of looting by soldiers of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or any of its subordinate units was discussed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: There was a discussion immediately after the events in Ovnak. This is a document that we have here. We had been accused, or rather they had said -- there were accusations that individual members of the 7th had been involved in looting. I know that the insignia of the 7th Muslim Brigade had been abused. We had insignia that would be worn on our shoulders, and I know that quite frequently thieves who weren't members of any unit would wear uniforms and would wear this insignia. And we were most frequently accused for their acts, especially after Ovnak. As far as Vares is concerned, accusations were made only later on, after we had left the area. I know that these rumours were spread for about 10 or 15 days, but I don't understand how someone can accuse us of having engaged in looting since on the 6th we all left the area of Vares municipality and then the 2nd Corps units took charge of the town. There were discussions, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I appreciate your answer, sir, but my question again: Did you -- I take it the answer is no, but did you have any discussions or were you present at any meetings of the senior leadership of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the immediate vicinity of Vares in the first week of November 1993 in which the subject by looting of soldiers within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was discussed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: A discussion was held, and at the discussion, that meeting, it was stated that looting was strictly prohibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After the unit -- after the brigade withdrew to the Zenica area, you've told us about meeting with the commander, Amir Kubura, on the 6th in Zenica. At that point in time or shortly thereafter were you present at meetings of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in which the subject of looting by members of that unit in the area of Vares was discussed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed that subject on the 6th and afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you recall any of the specific discussions that were held concerning looting by soldiers of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Vares which were attended or meetings which were attended by the commander of the brigade, Amir Kubura? Do you recall any of the specifics?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir, it's a bit unclear to me so I'll ask you this question: Did any soldiers of any subordinate units of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade enter the city of Vares proper or the town of Vares proper?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: When I said that I and members of my command entered the town together with my reconnaissance platoon, upon entering the town of Vares or that part of Vares, Majdan -- well, as I said, we were in Vares Majdan. We entered a cafe; it had been abandoned. There was coffee, there were juices, some cakes in the cafe, and we spent three or four hours there and helped ourselves to what we could find. On that day I had a problem with a soldier who had taken 50 kilos of flour, put it on his back, threw down his rifle, and said, I'm going home; my family is starving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: When you say that you entered the town of Vares or that part of Vares Majdan, did you or any of the soldiers of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade travel farther north from Vares Majdan into the centrum or centre of Vares town itself?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps one of my soldiers went there, but I didn't. I in fact don't really know Vares. So when you ask me about the centre, I don't know what the centre would be in that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of having attended any of the other meetings with the leaders of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, whether any of the soldiers from the 2rd or 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade entered Vares proper?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the 3rd Battalion entered the town late in the afternoon because there was incessant fighting in the forested part of Vares Majdan. I know that part of the 2nd Battalion also entered Vares Majdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, that they entered the town late in the afternoon, can you tell us which day you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the 4th. But this has to do with the meeting of three battalion commanders in an area, the diameter of which was about 500 metres. And we stayed there until 4.00 in the afternoon at the latest. When I said that they entered late, I mean that it was between 1.00 and 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, sir, you've mentioned soldiers or members of the 3rd Battalion -- the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade entering Vares Majdan. Do you know or did you become aware from attendance of meetings of the command whether any of the soldiers of the 2nd and 3rd Battalions of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade travelled further north from Vares Majdan into Vares itself?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they probably advance further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. I'm about to move into a different subject that I think will take us a little bit longer than five minutes. It is the last area. I expect I only need about 10 to 15 minutes to complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how much do you believe you will need afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 10 to 15 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's 5.25 and we will resume at about 10 to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I reviewed my notes. I did have a couple of follow-on questions and then we'll move on to my last subject. But this map that you have to your right showing the campaign in and around the area of Vares, you told us who was the person who actually made that map. And I'm wondering if you can again tell us that person's name.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Saban Zunic. On this time on the 4th and 5 he was the assistant Chief of Staff for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "assistant Chief of Staff for operations and training," that was within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, the place that's marked on the map and that you've told us about several times, Strijezevo, was there in fact a forward command post, an IKM, of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade at that location in early November 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: There was a forward command post of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the village of Strijezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, you've told us that that location is the one where you met with the brigade commander, Amir Kubura, in early November 1993. And I'm wondering if you can tell us how many other members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade staff were present at that forward command post in the first few days of November 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: There was the brigade commander, Amir Kubura, the deputy commander, Halil Brzina. The Chief of Staff Serif Patkovic wasn't there. There was the assistant Chief of Staff for operations and training, Saban Zunic. There was the assistant commander for logistics, Azar Bektas. As for the others, I'm not sure whether it's necessary for me to mention their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine. Would it be fair, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I see my learned friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think there's an error in the transcript. When -- the witness said that the Chief of Staff wasn't there, whereas the transcript states the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'll clarify that, sir. To the best of your recollection, the Chief of Staff Serif Patkovic was not present at the forward command post in Strijezevo in early November 1993. Is that correct? He was not there to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Would it be fair to say, sir, that the persons who were there represented a significant portion of the senior leadership of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn then, sir, to the final topic I'd like to discuss with you. You told us earlier this afternoon, this is reflected in the transcript at page 16, lines 14 through 20, you told us, sir, that the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the first few months of 1993, Asim Koricic, left at some point in the beginning of April 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know where Mr. Asim Koricic went when he left at the beginning of April or in the beginning of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Not officially. I do know where he went in a private capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you elaborate on that answer for us, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he left - and this is what others have told me - he went to visit families, or his family in Austria at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us also that in the fall of 1993, I believe you said September, you again saw Mr. Asim Koricic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: From the time period, sir, that Asim Koricic left in the beginning of April 1993 until the time period when you next saw him in September 1993, Amir Kubura was responsible for day-to-day operations of running the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Officially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in fact, sir, in the first week of August 1993, Amir Kubura was formally appointed as the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At any point in time after he left in April 1993, did -- until the end of the war as far as you know, did Asim Koricic perform the duties of commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: After the time that he left in the beginning of April 1993 until the end of the war, did Asim Koricic exercise command functions with respect to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At any point in time after he left in April 1993 until Amir Kubura was appointed formally as the commander in August 1993, were you aware of any orders for the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade issued by Mr. Asim Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: On the 9th of December, I was handing over the duties of commander of the battalion to Mr. Adilovic in Travnik, and I know that on that day, the 9th of December, except for me there was also Ahmet Adilovic who was the then-assistant commander for morale -- well, there was also Semir Terzic who handed over as an operations officer and an officer from the intelligence service. So Asim Koricic left to go to the Travnik battalion together with these people. The formal command, in the legal sense of the word, was in the hands of Enver Adilovic, as far as that particular battalion was concerned. But the real role of commander and the real orders were being issued by Asim Koricic all the way up until mid-February when that same battalion was used to set up a separate brigade. The reason why they left the brigade and the reason why they left to Travnik, my own personal opinion is this about the whole story: I do know that there was some obstruction on his part when he was issuing commands within the brigade especially at that time. I also know that Ahmet Adilovic as assistant commander for morale often misused the stamp and the possibility of signing documents. And one of the reasons for their departure in the same way -- and there's something else I have forgotten to say. In the same period of time, on the 9th of December, the assistant commander for security Nesib Talic also handed over his duties. The reason for their departure -- his departure as well, was that it was finally discovered what was going on at the music school. There were certain indications and more or less proof that this person never reported to the commander and that he misused the stamp, the possibility to sign documents, and his own position, and that he was always covering things up. So when you asked me whether he was a commander, yes, but Asim Koricic was the commander of that battalion from the middle of December to the middle of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back and start with the question that I actually asked. After April 1993, were any command functions with respect to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade being carried out by Asim Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've told us, sir - and I believe this is at page 40, line 7 - that after the 16th of March, 1993, you attended the briefings or daily meetings or regular meetings of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: After the 16th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe that's what the answer, as reflected in the English transcript said, on page 40, line 7.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At these meetings of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade that you attended after the 16th of March, 1993, who presided over these meetings?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Amir Kubura, Halil Brzina, and Ahmet Adilovic, depending.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that would depend on whether Amir Kubura was present, would it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Because if Amir Kubura were present as the senior-most de facto commander, he would be presiding over meetings of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But according to his position he was the highest ranking. But these powers had never formally been handed over to him. Was it simply about the departure of Asim Koricic? I don't know. I mean, I suppose I have to say the following here. Since we are talking about the brigade commander here and there was a war on and he had left the country, never mind where he went, Croatia, Slovenia, Austria, it doesn't really matter. But the approval to leave the country should have been granted by the then-supreme command staff. Nobody within the brigade knew of such an approval having been granted by anyone. The brigade had to continue to exist and to continue to do their job, and this is something you can see on the basis of this document. The battalion was at Travnik without any commander, and they were engaged in combat activity. And it was reflected on the situation in other municipalities, Zenica, all the way through the Kakanj and Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But, sir, that's actually -- you've actually hit on my very point. In a military unit, there's always someone who's in charge, whether it is based on a piece of paper or it's based on being the most senior officer present. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after Asim Koricic left in the beginning of April 1993, the Chief of Staff, Amir Kubura, took over as the commander of that 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: He took over only by the beginning of August. That's when he actually became commander. Up until then, he was the Chief of Staff and he signed everything as the Chief of Staff and also on behalf of Asim Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But he was exercising the functions of the commander of that brigade, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any point in time receive any instruction or order or directive from any higher authorities such as the 3rd Corps that you were to disregard any orders or documents signed by Amir Kubura because he wasn't authorised to sign such documents of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any point after Asim Koricic left in November or, excuse me, in April of 1993, did you ever have any contact from Mr. Koricic, whether by telephone or fax or by letter saying, in effect, Amir Kubura is not in charge, don't follow any orders that he issues?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I myself never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you hear, sir, of anyone else in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade having any such communication from Asim Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. But I do know that he was in touch with some senior officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say, sir, "senior officials," who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Ahmet Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And his role within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was what?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: He was the assistant commander for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And religious affairs?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No, just information and propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Based on the information that you have, were any other senior officials, as you put it, in contact or communication with Asim Koricic during the period of time that he was out of the country after the beginning of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Officially I don't know. I know things based on private statements by the aforementioned Adilovic, that he was in touch with him, but that he actually contacted officially anyone in the brigade, I do not know of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When Mr. Koricic returned to Central Bosnia in late 1993 or the autumn or winter of 1993, did he remain in Central Bosnia after that period of time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: He stayed in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, or are you aware of whether Mr. Asim Koricic suffered any negative consequences as a result of being out of Bosnia for a number of months in 1993 when he was still the formal commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you're not aware of any instance where he was disciplined or subject to any kind of prosecution or administrative action for being out of the area of responsibility for his brigade for many months in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a couple of short questions. Mr. Junuzovic, you said that Mr. Kubura in the beginning of August was made commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Kubura was made commander, the Chief of Staff was also appointed for the 7th Muslim Brigade. Do you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Within the framework of the same order, the appointment was made for the post of commander, deputy commander, and the Chief of Staff. The commander was Amir Kubura, the Chief of Staff -- or rather his deputy Halil Brzina, and the Chief of Staff, Serif Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about three -- people were three establishment duties?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When you got to Travnik, did soldiers ask you about Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. After my arrival to Travnik -- well, for about two months they had no real contact with the brigade except for brief telegrams through the operations group, Bosanska Krajina. They asked me where Asim Koricic was, where he had gone to, when he was coming back, why did he leave. They asked about who the new commander was, and I used to reply that there was no commander. But Amir Kubura as Chief of Staff was there, and then they asked questions about him, who he was, where he came from, and that sort of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did they know of Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to clarify matters with regard to questions put by my learned colleague of the Prosecution, did you yourself see any kind of looting or the destruction of property during the time that you were at Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As I said in reply to the question put to me by the Prosecution, what happened to me was that I saw one of my fighters grabbing a sack of flour, dropping his gun in front of me, and taking off in the direction of Breza. I don't know whether anyone else could have taken a bottle of oil or put something in their pockets or their rucksacks. I don't know. It may have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In this bundle of documents that you have in front of you, could you take a look at document number 11, also 12 and 13. Document number 11 is P478. Could you tell me who signed this document; do you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This is the signature of Saban Zunic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the same person who drew up and signed the map that you were looking at earlier on?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Does this order ban all members of the 7th Brigade from entering the city of Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the next document, number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, this is the document P449.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And I would just like you to look at item 4, or indent 4, starting on arrival to settlements, et cetera, inhabited settlements. Have you found it, on arrival, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Have you read through this passage?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by the commander of the 3rd Corps, Mehmed Alagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is it visible on the basis of this document if you read through the text of paragraph number 4?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Should I read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you read it for yourself and then you can comment, so as not to waste any time.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As to the 7th Muslim Brigade, he is referring to the fact that looting and the carrying off of goods was prevented thanks to the intervention of the military police and the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more document, please. It is number 13, and it is P450. The date is the 17th of November, 1993. Could you read through it and comment on it very briefly?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This comes from the supreme command staff and the commander's office, and it's signed by the deputy commander Jovan Divjak. And it is addressed to the command of the 2nd Corps and the 3rd Corps for information. The Ministry of the Interior has sent the armed forces supreme command staff document number 014190 of the 16th of November, 1993, which informed us that on the 16th of November, 1993, a 2nd Corps unit of, according to the MUP document, about 300 troops entered the city of Vares. And after arrival of that unit, individual cases of stealing and looting began.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Was the 7th Brigade in the area of Vares at that time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Junuzovic, is it correct that the supreme command staff appointed commanders of brigades as acting commanders, and the commanders were appointed by the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are taking the floor as part of the cross-examination or are you just asking additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you. Since we should have come in earlier, this question is not all that essential. Perhaps we will come back after the Judges' questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. I have a couple of questions of military nature strictly speaking to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In replying to questions earlier on, you had said that when there was an action there was a reconnaissance platoon which checks out the area ahead of the rest of the troops. Could you specify who exactly made up that reconnaissance platoon?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Primarily, if you think in a terms of a regular army, you would have the soldiers who are trained primarily for such reconnaissance tasks, who have been trained to gather certain data or who have good eyesight and good hearing and are experienced fighters. And you don't need to necessarily appoint people with a great deal of combat experience. Since such units are not primarily intended to engage in combat activity but to simply check out the area and gather as much data as possible and to locate the enemy positions and to provide that data to the relevant commands, to their superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it happen occasionally that that reconnaissance platoon also includes members of military police?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know -- well, I myself have not seen that in practice. I mean, we have not normally included such people in those platoons, but it may happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In replying to one of the questions at a certain point you dealt with the matter of fires in the course of combat operations. As far as you know, these units, fighting units, for example your battalion, did they own any incendiary devices or ammunitions or any fire launchers?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: My battalion did not have those and we did not have any ammunition which was likely to lead to the setting of any materials alight. Since this was a larger-calibre weaponry we are talking about, and we did not have that available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case how do you explain that in the course of those combat operations there were certain houses being set on fire? How could it happen technically speaking if you did not have any incendiary devices yourself?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In my statement, Your Honour, I only mentioned fire once in relation to the city of Vares. And as to Ovnak I said that there was damage done to buildings due to rifle or machine-gun ammunition. When our units entered Vares, they did not engage in any combat activity, we did not open fire of any sort, especially not using grenade launchers or Howitzers and that could have been possible -- in that case, it could have been possible to set that building on fire. And as to the area of Ovnak, I simply said that in the course of these combat operations in an inhabited settlement, buildings necessarily get damaged because people shoot from behind corners, house corners, from rooftops, through windows, from the stables or what have you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me move on to another topic. In replying to one of the questions earlier on you said that at a certain point at the music school there was one of your soldiers who had been detained there because he was drunk and you could not go and see him. For what reason, since you were a battalion commander, did you not have access to one of your soldiers who was -- one of the soldiers of your battalion? Could you perhaps clarify that. What obstacles did you encounter?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Since I thought that it was my duty to punish that soldier and that he should undergo a regular disciplinary procedure, I thought it was not necessary for him to be detained but that he should be sent to barracks in Travnik and that disciplinary measures should be imposed. So in my attempt to exempt him basically from this sort of treatment, first of all I was not allowed in, and afterwards when I talked to Mr. Talic he allowed it, I mean he relinquished the soldier. He sent him back to my battalion. But I was denied access because they said he was detained because of drunkenness and that required a more complex disciplinary procedure, and apparently as a battalion commander it was not within my area of competence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to take a look at the document prepared by the Defence, the document number 2. In the upper left-hand corner on the first page, what can you see? What does it say? "1700 hours, the 5th of June, 1993." What's marked above that reference?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The command, in inverted commas, it says tactical group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is a tactical group? Could you inform us -- could you provide us with information about this tactical group?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Within the military -- well, for example, you have a case you are dealing with here and that in the military organisation you have platoons, companies, battalions, and then brigades. Of course in an army a tactical group is a formation that is not a permanent formation; it is established only for the purposes of carrying out a given task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who has the power to establish a tactical group?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In this case I think that it's a superior body, a body superior to the 7th Muslim Brigade. All authority was transferred to the 7th Muslim Brigade. They were given the authority to create such a group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you have a look at document number 9, please. In the upper left-hand corner there is a stamp. What does the stamp say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It says military unit number 5083. Strictly confidential document number 1220/93. The date is the 3rd of November, 1993, in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you have a look at the last page of the document and could you have a look at the stamp next to Amir Kubura's signature. What does the stamp say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It says "military unit, 5083, Zenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is this military unit, 5083?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It's another name for the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade had another name then?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Not another name. It's the same in terms of military organisation. Apart from the names of brigades that are assigned, if you compare this to the way other armies are organised, you can have various names. You have regiments in Britain, and they have letters that they use as designations or numbers or the names of a town or a region, I'm referring to Great Britain. But in our country, units would first be allocated a number. In this case the 7th Muslim Brigade had the number 5083, military unit 5083.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for that information. Could you go back to the first page and could you tell us who this document was addressed to? I can see that in your language it says "komandant." Could you tell me who this document was addressed to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This document is called "planned for commander reconnaissance for the 5th of June," and it's addressed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read out the two first lines, and I can see that in your language it says "komandant" and then it says the 7th Brigade. We're still referring to document number 9.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have a look at document number 9 and could you tell me who this document is addressed to? It should be on the first page.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily. The procedure followed in our offices was such that the addressee might only be mentioned on the last page, and that is the case in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I can see on the first page that it says "komandant." Who is the document addressed to? I'm not talking about the last page; I'm talking about the first page. Because in English the translation states that it's to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade commander. I want to make sure that this corresponds to what it says in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does correspond to the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I would like to deal with the map that you have before you, and my last questions will relate to this map. Could the usher please adjust the map on the ELMO to make sure that we can see the name of the person who made the map. That's at the top. There we are. So at the top we have the date, the 4th of November, Vares, and I can see that it also says Saban. Is that the person that you mentioned who was the deputy in charge of operations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: He was the assistant Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was the assistant Chief of Staff. With the transcript -- according to the transcript you said that he was the deputy in charge of operations. When it says the 4th of November, 1993, does that mean that the markings on the map were made on the 4th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you then translate, or rather could you tell us what it -- what "radna karta komandanta" mean? What does "radna karta komandanta" mean?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This map was made to be a form of support for the written order I was issued with. In principle it's not always necessary to issue a written order if a given task has to be carried out. In this case, the commander could have made use of this map without having put anything down in writing, without having drafted a written order, and I would have known exactly what to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, sir. Who wrote down "1400 hours, the 5th of November." And I'll read out what it says in your language: "Pocetak, 1400 hours." Who wrote that down?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Probably Saban Zunic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what does that mean? He signed on the 4th of November. Is he providing an account of the situation on the 5th of November? Because what we can see after -- further below, does that refer to the situation, 1400 hours on the 5th of November?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: He made this map on the 4th of November. He made it for the attack that was to commence at 1400 hours on the 5th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can have a look as to what has been noted on the right. What can we see on the right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It says "vojna tajna," it says military secret, strictly confidential, and we have the code name below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this military operation of the 5th of November had the code name EL1F. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What else is being marked in black capital letters? As far as I can remember, it also said "komandant" at the bottom to the right. That's correct. My memory is quite good. Who wrote that down?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Saban Zunic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why did he write this name down? Does it mean that the map was to go to the commander, Amir Kubura? What is the meaning of this reference to commander Amir Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: In this case, this was to be the commander's working map; that's what it says. My copy was only to contain reference to myself as the addressee. It shouldn't have said "working map."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the battalion commander, did you have a copy of this map?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my very last question: Does this mean that when there is a military operation, one necessarily has such a map?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when you do have such a map, is there a reference to all the units that are present in the field?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Usually, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no reference to the units involved?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Units are referred to only if it concerns them, and if it concerns units who are being assigned a task in relation to the map that is made for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we can see -- Mr. Usher, could you adjust the map so we can see the units involved in the action. Very well. We can see 1MBB, so that is the 1st Battalion which is engaged in action. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when there is a military action, one refers to the theoretical advance of the units engaged in combat in the field?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'll now conclude. The forward post where it says 7M, 1MBB, is that the forward command post? Could you point to it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the reference to the left, what does it mean? To the left there is a little flag with a triangle.

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: This little flag here stands for the forward command post of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And to the left, what does that sign stand for?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It stands for my command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's your post. So how is it that we know that the 1st Battalion that will advance toward the positions to the right, whereas your post is behind the forward command post? How do you explain that? Wouldn't the situation usually be the other way around?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: You have -- you are right. There was probably a mistake made here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that we have a mistake there, because in theory you would be in front of the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. The way my forward command post has been depicted is what was the mistake. It shouldn't have been marked there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where should your post have been?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It should have been marked with the unit's symbol. It should have shown how it was advancing in accordance with the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You told us that you were in Vares Majdan. Is that correct? You didn't enter Vares. You were in a place that is just before Vares?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you point to the location, could you point to the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have another 15 minutes. Do -- are there any other questions that either of the Judges would like to ask? Yes, we have some other questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: I have only one question on a document that you have seen that is number 9 in your map of documents. Could you take it -- I'm sorry. I apologise. I meant to mention number 7. In this document the 7th Brigade is defending itself against allegations of looting and burning of private property, and we have discussed paragraph 4 of this document and you have confirmed the content of what is said there, you left the area after the battle. I'm interested now in putting you a question on point 3 of the same document. It says: "The most illustrative example of our members attitude towards property is the church in Brajkovici and the monastery in Kraljeva Sutjeska which have not been touched." This afternoon I heard you saying, and hence my question in response of a question of the Defence counsel for Mr. Kubura that your brigade -- the 7th Brigade and your battalion did not enter Brajkovici. So there seems to be a contradiction between what you said this afternoon and the content of point 3 of the -- this document. And could you help me out?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: When I answered that question, I didn't say that my battalion was there. During this period, I was not the battalion commander but I was a member of the brigade command, and I was present in the Ovnak area. I know that on that very same day UNPROFOR and EU monitors visited Brajkovici and the church referred to. I know that there were rumours according to which it hadn't been damaged. They filmed and photographed the building, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: That's right. But you've said on page 30 -- 31 and the beginning of page 32, the question of counsel for the Defence is the following: "Mr. Junuzovic, could you tell the Trial Chamber whether members of the 2nd or the 3rd Battalion, when it came to these combat activities, ever entered the village of Brajkovici?" And your answer is: "They didn't." Now, this document seems to suggest that they were present there and that they did not do nasty things to the church in Brajkovici, but that suppose that they have been present there. So could you please help me out there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: The question had to do with members of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion, and they really weren't down there. After UNPROFOR arrived, a military police platoon, or rather one patrol was sent with them to go to Brajkovici and to check things out. But the army did not go and did not accompany the monitors and UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand your answer better now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, the map we were talking about that was made by Mr. Saban Zunic only has markings with respect to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, yet you've told us about the presence of the 2nd and 3rd Battalions as well. Just so we're clear, sir: This map was specifically produced for the benefit of you as the 1st Battalion commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: It was made for the commander. It was to serve as his working map, as you can see from the title, and it only concerned the engagement of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. There may or may not have been similar maps for the 2nd and 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET JUNUZOVIC
utterances.text: I doubt that that was the case for that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
